uncited: It builds on [Bayesian Inference Surrogate Framework](11307-bayesian-inference-surrogate-framework.md) by applying Bayesian inference to obtain the posterior distribution over parameters conditioned on a user-specified spatial feature.
*   $W^{(t)}$: A 2D tensor of shape $(N, J)$. $W^{(t)}_{i,j}$ represents the continuous rendering weight contributed by Gaussian $i$ to label $j$ in frame $t$.
It bounds the maximum evidence injected per frame.
Gaussians with total weight below this are not decayed.
*   **Closed-Loop Feedback:** In a closed-loop system, rendered label maps drive next-frame association, potentially reinforcing early errors.
*   **Injection Bound:** The update satisfies $\eta^{(t)}_i \cdot W^{(t)}_i < \tau$ for $\tau > 0, S_i \ge 0, W^{(t)}_i \ge 0$.
*   **When to Use:** When using continuous rendering weights for evidence accumulation in a closed-loop system where early errors can be reinforced.
*   **When Not to Use:** When discrete counts are sufficient and closed-loop feedback is not a concern.
